questions.q: A crate of fruits contains one spoiled fruit for every 25 fruits. 60% of the spoiled fruits were sold. If the seller had sold 48 spoiled fruits, then the number of fruits in the crate were?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Line ko dhyan se padh: "One spoiled fruit for every 25 fruits". Iska matlab hai Spoiled aur Total fruits ka exact ratio 1:25 hai (1:26 mat kar dena).

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai, Spoiled fruits ka $60\%$ (yani $\frac{3}{5}$) 48 hai.
$$Total Spoiled = 48 \times \frac{5}{3} = 80$$
Ratio humara $1:25$ (Spoiled:Total) chal hi raha hai.
Total Fruits $= 80 \times 25 = 2000$.
Koi dum nahi tha calculation me, bas language ka khel tha.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Agar usne bola hota "one spoiled fruit for every 25 good fruits", toh ratio 1:26 banta. Bas yahi chhoti reading mistake bachcho ka $-0.5$ karwa deti hai.

Exam Takeaway: "For every X fruits" (matlab base X hai) aur "for every X good fruits" (matlab base X+1 hai) ka trap samajhna seekh le.

Reading TrapLogic
"For every 25 fruits"This means the ratio of Spoiled to Total is 1:25.

questions.q: The ratio between expenditure and saving is x:y. when income is increased by $15\%$, expenditure is increased by $20\%$ and savings are increased by $12\%$. Find the new ratio of expenditure and savings ?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: JSM / Alligation

Pen-Free Observation: Income hamesha Exp aur Sav ka combined effect hoti hai, direct Alligation thok.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Alligation: E(+20), S(+12), middle mein I(+15). Ratio of original E:S $= (15-12):(20-15) = 3:5$. Old Exp $= 300$, Sav $= 500$. New Exp $= 300$ pe $20\%$ badhakar $360$. New Sav $= 500$ pe $12\%$ badhakar $560$. Naya ratio $= 360:560 = 9:14$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): JSM se equations banayega $20x + 12y = 15(x+y)$, toh wahi $5x = 3y \Rightarrow x/y = 3/5$ milega. Lamba method hai.

Exam Takeaway: Mixture of percentages mein aankh band karke alligation pattern lagaya kar.

questions.q: A person wants to buy 10 chairs. The total cost of 10 chairs is Rs. 4,500. After bargaining, the shopkeeper agrees to decrease the cost of each chair by 20%. Then, the person purchased 10% more chairs. What will be the cost of the chairs that he purchased?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, ₹450 ki 1 chair aayi. $20\%$ (₹90) discount se ab ₹360 ki mili. $10$ pe $10\%$ jyada yani 11 chairs li. Ab bas $360 \times 11$ nikalna hai. 11 ka hack lagao aur seedha ans uthao.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Rate nikal kar new quantity se multiply, aur 11 ki vedic trick use karo.

Mathematically :-
$$Old \ Rate = \frac{4500}{10} = 450 \\\\ New \ Rate = 450 \times 0.80 = 360 \\\\ New \ Qty = 10 \times 1.1 = 11 \\\\ Total \ Cost = 360 \times 11 = 3960$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Total value par calculate kar ke values jodna.

Mathematically :-
$$Old \ Rate = 450 \Rightarrow Discount = 90 \\\\ Cost \ of \ 10 \ chairs = 10 \times 360 = 3600 \\\\ Cost \ of \ 1 \ extra = 360 \\\\ Total = 3600 + 360 = 3960$$

Exam Takeaway: Calculation hacks jaha applicable hon hamesha waha use karo, CGL/Bank exam me bohot faida dete hain.

questions.q: In an examination, (A + 6)% of the students failed in Mathematics and (A - 8)% failed in Science. 28% of the students failed in both the subjects. If the percentage of students who passed in both the subjects was 50%, then what is the value of A?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, total bachhe humesha $100\%$ hote hain. Jo dono subjects me pass hue wo $50\%$ de rakhe hain, toh iska matlab jo kisi na kisi ek me (ya dono me) fail hue wo total $100 - 50 = 50\%$ honge. Seedha set theory yaad kar.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Universal set wala formula laga aur equation turant solve kar de!

Mathematically :-
$$n(M \cup S) = n(M) + n(S) - n(M \cap S)$$
$$50 = (A + 6) + (A - 8) - 28$$
$$50 = 2A - 30 \implies 2A = 80 \implies A = 40$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Venn diagram ke logic se only math aur only science ke fail nikal ke total bana le.

Mathematically :-
$$\text{Only Math} = (A + 6) - 28 = A - 22$$
$$\text{Only Sci} = (A - 8) - 28 = A - 36$$
$$\text{Total Fail} = (A - 22) + (A - 36) + 28 = 2A - 30$$
$$2A - 30 = 50 \implies A = 40$$

Exam Takeaway: Har baar Venn diagram draw karne me time barbaad mat kiya kar, seedha union wala set formula dimag me rakha kar!

List IList II
Total Union$n(A \cup B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A \cap B)$

questions.q: In an examination every question correctly answered fetches two marks and for every question wrongly answered one mark is deducted. Anusha and Preet took the examination. Anusha attempted a certain number of question and 20\% of them went wrong. Preet attempted a certain number of questions and 10\% of the questions attempted by him went wrong. Anusha got 33 marks more than the pass mark and Preet got 48 marks more than the pass mark. Anusha and Preet together attempted 100 questions. What is the pass mark of the examination?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Expected Value & Divisibility.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, jab bhi correct aur incorrect ka percentage given ho, toh fraction se ek "Base Score Unit" nikal le. Uss unit se seedha divisibility check kar ke options eliminate karna sabse BEST approach hai. Warna original mock solution wale expected value (net marks) se linear equation banegi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Option Picking with Divisibility. Anusha ka 20\% (1/5) wrong hai, yani har 5 attempt ki packet me 4 right aur 1 wrong. Uska 1 packet ka marks = $4 \times (+2) + 1 \times (-1) = 7$ marks. Preet ka 10\% (1/10) wrong hai, yani har 10 attempt me 9 right aur 1 wrong. Uska 1 packet ka marks = $9 \times (+2) + 1 \times (-1) = 17$ marks. Total scores definitely 7 aur 17 ke multiples honge. Option se pass marks 37 uthao.

Mathematically :-
$$A_{score} = 37 + 33 = 70 \ (10 \times 7 \text{ units} \rightarrow 50 \text{ Qs}) \\ P_{score} = 37 + 48 = 85 \ (5 \times 17 \text{ units} \rightarrow 50 \text{ Qs}) \\ Total = 50 + 50 = 100 \text{ (Verified)}$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Original Mock Solution. Har attempt ka ek average expected mark nikal le decimals me.

Mathematically :-
$$A_{net} = 0.8(2) - 0.2(1) = 1.4 \\ P_{net} = 0.9(2) - 0.1(1) = 1.7 \\ P_{score} - A_{score} = 48 - 33 = 15 \\ 1.7(100 - A) - 1.4A = 15 \\ 170 - 3.1A = 15 \rightarrow 3.1A = 155 \rightarrow A = 50 \\ Pass = 50 \times 1.4 - 33 = 37$$

Exam Takeaway: Hamesha percentage ko packet ratio me tod kar unit score nikal le. Phir sidha options me margin add karke divisibility test kar. Ye DIRECT approach time 10x bacha legi bina kisi variable assume kiye!

questions.q: Every day, a wholesale fruit vendor sells $60 \%$ of his total stock. From the remaining stock, he donates $25 \%$ to a local orphanage, and then $20 \%$ of the rest gets spoiled overnight. If exactly 3720 fruits were spoiled over the first two nights combined, how many fruits did he start with on the first day?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, yahan lagatar 3 reductions ho rahe hain har roz. Pehle $60 \%$ bika, fir bache hue ka $25 \%$ daan kiya, fir jo bacha uska $20 \%$ kharab hua. Fractions ka series lamba hai, isliye $100$ ke bajaye $10000$ base maan le taaki calculations decimals me na phase.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Total stock ko ek aisi unit maan lo jo har fraction se easily divide ho jaye. Phir step-by-step successive decrease laga do.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Let Initial Stock} = 10000 \text{ units} \\ \text{Day 1: Sells } 60 \% \implies \text{Remaining} = 4000 \\ \text{Donates } 25 \% \text{ of } 4000 = 1000 \implies \text{Rest} = 3000 \\ \text{Night 1 Spoils} = 20 \% \text{ of } 3000 = 600 \\ \text{Day 2 Starts with} = 3000 - 600 = 2400 \text{ units} \\ \text{Day 2: Sells } 60 \% \text{ of } 2400 = 1440 \implies \text{Remaining} = 960 \\ \text{Donates } 25 \% \text{ of } 960 = 240 \implies \text{Rest} = 720 \\ \text{Night 2 Spoils} = 20 \% \text{ of } 720 = 144 \\ \text{Total Spoiled} = 600 + 144 = 744 \text{ units} \\ 744 \text{ units} = 3720 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = 5 \\ \text{Total initial fruits} = 10000 \times 5 = 50000 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Multipliers ko club karke single remaining fraction nikal lo jisse daily calculation aadhi ho jaye.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Let Initial Stock} = X \\ \text{Daily Rest Fraction (before spoiling)} = (1 - 0.60) \times (1 - 0.25) \\ = 0.40 \times 0.75 = 0.30 \\ \text{Night 1 Spoiled} = 20 \% \text{ of } 0.30X = 0.06X \\ \text{Remaining for Day 2} = 0.30X - 0.06X = 0.24X \\ \text{Night 2 Spoiled} = 20 \% \text{ of } (0.30 \times 0.24X) = 0.0144X \\ \text{Total Spoiled} = 0.06X + 0.0144X = 0.0744X \\ 0.0744X = 3720 \implies X = \frac{3720}{0.0744} = 50000 $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab din me multi-step reductions hon, toh un sabko club karke ek single remaining multiplier ($0.4 \times 0.75 = 0.3$) bana lena chahiye. Isse next day ki chain equation bohot choti aur fast ho jati hai.

questions.q: In an election between three candidates, the third-placed candidate received 1000 valid votes. From the remaining votes, the elected candidate received 5000 more votes than the runner-up candidate, accounting for $52\%$ of the total votes cast. If $16\%$ of votes were declared invalid (given that all the voters cast their vote), then the total number of cast votes was?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, variables ko total ke percentage terms me rakh kar equation balance karni hai, seedha $20x$ ki value aayegi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): W aur R ka gap base pakad. Mathematically :-
$$52x - (84x - 52x - 1000) = 5000$$
$$20x = 4000 \Rightarrow 100x = 20000$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Tree distribution method. Mathematically :-
$$Valid = 100x - 16x = 84x$$
$$W + R + 1000 = 84x$$
$$R = 32x - 1000$$
$$W - R = 5000$$
$$20x = 4000 \Rightarrow x = 200 \Rightarrow 100x = 20000$$

Method 3: 52% W ko toh Runner ko 52%-5k ATQ winner ko 52% mila total ka means valid ka bhi 52% hai ye absolute percentage hota hai never got confused. So apna 100% method lgao 52% + (52%-5k) + 1000 +16%I.V. = 100% TOTAL

Exam Takeaway: Election wale questions me tree diagram dimaag me set rakh aur ek hi variable me sab solve kar de.

questions.q: Deepak spends 75% of his income, whereas Karan spends 80% of his income. Both of them save Rs. 7,500 each. The income of Sanjay is one-third of the sum of the income of Deepak and Karan. If Sanjay spends (7/9)th of his income, then find his savings.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: 5. Unitary Scaling

Dekh bhai aise karna hai, dono methods se pura bhaukaal tight rakhte hain.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique - Actual Base calculation):
Deepak spends 75%, so saves 25% (\\frac{1}{4}). Base Income = $7500 \\times 4 = 30000$.
Karan spends 80%, so saves 20% (\\frac{1}{5}). Base Income = $7500 \\times 5 = 37500$.
Sum of Incomes = $30000 + 37500 = 67500$.
Sanjay's Income = $\\frac{67500}{3} = 22500$.
Sanjay spends $\\frac{7}{9}$, so saves $\\frac{2}{9}$.
Savings = $\\frac{2}{9} \\times 22500 = 5000$.

Method 2 (Teri 'Zeher' Ratio Approach):
Savings barabar hain, seedha ratios equate kar!
$D \\times 25\\% = K \\times 20\\% \\Rightarrow \\frac{D}{K} = \\frac{4}{5}$. Total = 9 units.
Sanjay's savings in units = $9 \\times \\frac{1}{3} \\times \\frac{2}{9} = \\frac{2}{3}$ units.
Ab real value se link kar: Deepak's saving = $4 \\times \\frac{1}{4} = 1$ unit.
Question ke hisaab se, $1 \\text{ unit} = 7500$.
Sanjay's saving = $7500 \\times \\frac{2}{3} = 5000$. Dono hi method 15 second wale hain, zero algebraic variables ka masterstroke!

Examiner yahi trap set karta hai. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Reduction $12\%$ ki hui aur amount me $2100$ ki. Yani $12\% = 2100$. $1\% = \frac{2100}{12} = 175$. Total bill $100\% = 17500$ ka tha. Par usne reduction ke baad pay kiya hai na! Toh $17500 - 2100 = 15400$. Option C (17500) mat mark kar dena jaldbazi me! Method 2 (Concept Builder): Ek aur direct tarika dekh. Tujhe 'Paid' amount puchi hai. Agar $12\%$ ki chhoot mili, toh pay kitna kiya? $88\%$. Agar $12\% = 2100$, toh $88\% = \frac{2100}{12} \times 88 = 175 \times 88 = 15400$. Seedha ek step me aagaya answer! Exam Takeaway: Language ko last word tak dhyan se padh. questions.q: A student appeared in 6 papers. The maximum marks are the same for each paper. His marks in these papers are in the proportion 5 : 6 : 7 : 8 : 9 : 10. Overall he scored 60%. In how many papers he received less than 60% marks?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling / Deviation

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Data proportion me diya hai aur final relative constraint (60%) par focus hai. Total marks obtained ratio ke terms me jodo, waha se maximum marks ki imaginary value nikal lo.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Sum of scores = $5+6+7+8+9+10 = 45x$. Ye 45x overall max marks ka 60% hai. Yaani $60\% = 45x \implies 100\% (Total Max) = \frac{45x}{60} \times 100 = 75x$. 6 papers ka Total Max 75x hai, aur sab equal hain. Toh 1 paper ka Max = $\frac{75x}{6} = 12.5x$. Kisi subject me 60% se kam aane ka constraint check karna hai. 12.5x ka 60% hota hai 7.5x. Toh kin subjects me 7.5x se kam hai? Pehle teen (5, 6, 7). Answer 3.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Algebraically assume Total Max = 600. Then 60% = 360. $45x = 360 \implies x=8$. Marks are 40, 48, 56, 64, 72, 80. Each paper max = 100. 60% of 100 = 60. Marks < 60 are 40, 48, 56 (3 papers). Same logic!

Best Exam Approach: Method 1 me ek ratio base calculation hai jo dimag me jaldi process hota hai.

If as a result of this, the sales of tickets increases his weekly collection by 25200. Then find by what value did the gross collection increase per day?

Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change (The Chain Reaction) - TRICK IDENTIFICATION

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, examiner maje le raha hai. Start percentages se kara par ant me sidha rupay me value de di. Toh hum kyu formula lagayen? Divisibility by $7$ ka khel hai bas.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Ye question pura scam hai! Pucha hai 'increase per day'! Toh bhai mere, seedha $1$ hafte ke collection ko $7$ se divide karna tha! Aankhein khuli rakh paper me! Mathematically :- $$ \text{Increase per day} = \frac{\text{Weekly Increase}}{7} \\ \text{Increase} = \frac{25200}{7} = 3600 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Agar tum concept pe gaye toh net effect nikaloge, fir equation solve karoge. Itna bada trap bicha rakha hai wahan mat fans jana. Mathematically :- $$ \text{Net } \% = -15 + 35 - \frac{15 \times 35}{100} = +14.75\% \\ 14.75\% \text{ of Total} = 25200 \text{ (Useless calc)} \\ \text{Per day} = \frac{25200}{7} = 3600 $$

questions.q: A fraction $\frac{3}{5}$ is decreased by $\frac{2}{5}$. The resulting fraction is then increased by 20%.\n\nWhat is the percentage decrease/increase in the value of the original fraction?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, base me 5 hai dono jagah. $ rac{3}{5}$ me se $ rac{2}{5}$ gaya toh bacha $ rac{1}{5}$. Ab $ rac{1}{5}$ ko 20% (yani khud ka $ rac{1}{5}$th) badhana hai. Seedha seedha base ko 25 dimaag me soch aur numerators ko 15 aur 6 padh. 15 se 6 hua, matlab 9 ka loss 15 par. $ rac{9}{15}$ seedha 60% hota hai! Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Base same kar lo taaki fractions integers jaise behave karein. Mathematically :-
$ ext{Original} = rac{3}{5} = rac{15}{25}$
$ ext{New} = ( rac{3}{5} - rac{2}{5}) imes 1.2 = rac{1}{5} imes rac{6}{5} = rac{6}{25}$
$\% ext{ Decrease} = rac{15 - 6}{15} imes 100 = 60\%$ Method 2 (Concept Builder): Basic se chalte hain. Pehle original fraction me se fraction minus karo, fir jo aaye usko 20% increase karo (multiply by $ rac{6}{5}$). Mathematically :-
$ ext{Original} = rac{3}{5}$
$ ext{After subtraction} = rac{3}{5} - rac{2}{5} = rac{1}{5}$
$ ext{After 20\% increase} = rac{1}{5} imes (1 + rac{20}{100}) = rac{1}{5} imes rac{6}{5} = rac{6}{25}$
$ ext{Absolute Change} = rac{3}{5} - rac{6}{25} = rac{15}{25} - rac{6}{25} = rac{9}{25}$
$ ext{Percentage Change} = rac{ rac{9}{25}}{ rac{15}{25}} imes 100 = rac{9}{15} imes 100 = 60\%$ Exam Takeaway: Is type ke questions me "decreased by a fraction" aur "decreased by a percentage" ka phrasing hi trap hota hai. Hamesha final aur initial fraction ka base same kar lo (jaise yahan humne dono ko 25 bana liya), toh calculation seconds me muh-zabani ho jayegi.

questions.q: In company A, the number of male employees is $71.42\%$ of the total employees. The total number of employees in company B is $14.28\%$ less than that in company A. If the difference between male and female employees in company A is $(x+12)$ and the total employees in company B is 84, find the value of x.
questions.s:
The "Pen-Free" Observation First:

Dekh bhai, fractions strong hone chahiye. $14.28\% = \frac{1}{7}$ and $71.42\% = \frac{5}{7}$. Bas en fraction scale par relation bitha aur ek line me solve kar!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):

Mathematically :-

$$ 14.28\% = \frac{1}{7}, \quad 71.42\% = \frac{5}{7} \\ B = \left(1 - \frac{1}{7}\right)A = \frac{6}{7}A \\ 84 = \frac{6}{7}A \implies A = 98 \\ \text{Males (A)} = \frac{5}{7} \times 98 = 70 \\ \text{Females (A)} = 98 - 70 = 28 \\ \text{Diff} = 70 - 28 = 42 \\ (x + 12) = 42 \implies x = 30 $$

Exam Takeaway: Standard percentages ko directly fraction me todna TCS exams me life-saver hai.

questions.q: The number of peacocks in a bird sanctuary was P in the year 2000. The number decreased by $10\%$ in the next decade and increased by $50\%$ in the decade after that. If the difference between the number of peacocks in the years 2020 and 2000 is 5250, and it increased by $36\%$ in the next half decade, then what is the number of peacocks in the year 2025?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, pehle gira fir utha. Net successive change nikal, P ki value aayegi. Uske baad 2025 ki value aayegi jo 1.36 se multiply karke banegi, jiska DS 9 HOGA COZ +18/50 SO opt C&D elmnt and unit digit pakad lena hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Net effect = 0.9 x 1.5 = 1.35. Yani 35% bada. $35\% = 5250$ toh $100\% (P) = 15000$. 2020 me = $15000 \times 1.35 = 20250$. Naya 36% bada, $20250 \times 1.36$. Last digit zero ke baad 4 aayega, option B me 40 hai, seedha tick maar!

Mathematically :-
$\text{Net}_1 = 0.9 \times 1.5 = 1.35$
$\text{Diff} = 35\% = 5250 \implies 100\% = 15000$
$P_{2020} = 15000 \times 1.35 = 20250$
$P_{2025} = 20250 \times 1.36 = 27540$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): $P - P(0.9)(1.5)$ likh ke formula banayega, subtract karega toh bhi end me calculation unit digit se hi fast hogi.

Mathematically :-
$P(1.5)(0.9) - P = 5250$
$0.35P = 5250 \implies P = 15000$
$P_{2025} = 15000(1.35)(1.36) = 27540$

Exam Takeaway: Pure multiplication mat kar, Unit digit aur Digital Sum hamesha bachate hain successive problems me.

questions.q: Raman saves $x\%$ of her income. If her income increases by $16\%$ and expenditure increases by $10\%$ then her savings increased by $50\%$. What is the value of x?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 3. JSM / Deviation (Cross-Product Alligation)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, Income me bas $16\%$ ka hike hai, aur Saving achanak $50\%$ ud gayi, jabki Expenditure me halka sa $10\%$ change hai. Iska seedha matlab hai initially saving ka share total income me bahut kam tha.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Seedha Alligation laga! Exp ($10\%$) aur Sav ($50\%$) mix hokar total Income ($16\%$) ka change banate hain. Secondon ka game hai!

Mathematically :-
$$ E = 10\\% , \\ S = 50\\% , \\ I = 16\\% \\\\ Ratio (E:S) = (50-16) : (16-10) \\\\ = 34 : 6 = 17 : 3 \\\\ Total \\ I = 17 + 3 = 20 \\\\ S\\% = \\frac{3}{20} \\times 100 = 15\\% $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Maan le Total Income $= 100$, Sav $= x$, Exp $= 100-x$. Equation set kar: Naya Exp $+$ Nayi Sav $=$ Nayi Income. Par ye gadha majdoori hai.

Mathematically :-
$$ I = 100, \\ S = x, \\ E = 100-x \\\\ E_{new} + S_{new} = I_{new} \\\\ 1.1(100-x) + 1.5x = 116 \\\\ 110 - 1.1x + 1.5x = 116 \\\\ 0.4x = 6 \\\\ x = 15\\% $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab bhi $3$ components (A, B, aur unka combined total) ka percentage increase/decrease diya ho, Alligation se fast kuch nahi hota!

questions.q: Everyday a vegetable vendor sells $1/2$ of his total stock. $10 \%$ of the remaining stock overnight gets spoiled. If 1983 vegetables spoiled over 3 nights in total, then how many vegetables did he start with on the first day?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change

Pen-Free Observation: Har roz half sell hota hai aur fir bache hue half ka $10 \%$ (yani remaining part) spoil hota hai. Fraction chain lagatar change ho rahi hai toh calculation thodi lengthy lag sakti hai, best hai koi constant value assume karna.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Denominators dekhte hue initial value ko 8000 ka koi multiple maan lo ($2 \times 10 \times 2 \times 10$ series ke hisab se) taaki points me calculations na jaye.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Let Initial Stock} = 8000 \text{ units} \\ \text{Day 1:} \text{ sells } 4000, \text{ Rem } 4000. \text{ Night 1 spoils } 10 \% = 400 \\ \text{Day 2:} \text{ Starts with } 3600. \text{ Sells } 1800, \text{ Rem } 1800. \text{ Night 2 spoils } 10 \% = 180 \\ \text{Day 3:} \text{ Starts with } 1620. \text{ Sells } 810, \text{ Rem } 810. \text{ Night 3 spoils } 10 \% = 81 \\ \text{Total Spoiled} = 400 + 180 + 81 = 661 \text{ units} \\ 661 \text{ units} = 1983 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = 3 \\ \text{Total initial fruits} = 8000 \times 3 = 24000 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Pure fraction method laga kar $X$ le kar solve karna.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Let Initial} = X \\ \text{Night 1 Spoiled} = 10 \% \text{ of } \frac{X}{2} = \frac{400}{8000}X \\ \text{Remaining Day 2 Start} = \frac{X}{2} - \frac{X}{20} = \frac{9}{20}X \\ \text{Night 2 Spoiled} = 10 \% \text{ of } (\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{9}{20}X) = \frac{180}{8000}X \\ \text{Remaining Day 3 Start} = \frac{9}{40}X - \frac{9}{400}X = \frac{81}{400}X \\ \text{Night 3 Spoiled} = 10 \% \text{ of } (\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{81}{400}X) = \frac{81}{8000}X \\ \text{Total Spoiled} = (\frac{400 + 180 + 81}{8000})X = \frac{661}{8000}X \\ \frac{661}{8000}X = 1983 \implies X = 24000 $$

questions.q: The water volume in a reservoir increases by $16 \frac{2}{3}\%$ in January, decreases by 20,000 liters in February, and increases by $25\%$ in March. If the final volume is exactly $25\%$ more than the initial volume, find the total increment in the volume during January.

Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change.

Seedha mind me strike karna chahiye ki February end me volume P thi . Ye Result hai Direct yaad karlo log isko short tirick bolenge baad me 🫠.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Reverse Gear.

Mathematically :-

$$ Final = 1.25P \\ Before\_Mar = \frac{1.25P}{1.25} = P \\ Before\_Feb = P + 20000 \\ Jan\_Inc = 16 \frac{2}{3}\% = \frac{1}{6} \\ \frac{7P}{6} = P + 20000 \\ \frac{P}{6} = 20000 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Forward Equation.

Mathematically :-

$$ \left(\frac{7P}{6} - 20000\right) \times \frac{5}{4} = \frac{5P}{4} \\ \frac{7P}{6} - 20000 = P \\ \frac{P}{6} = 20000 $$

Relation: New Income = New Exp + New Saving. $400 + 8x = 300 + 3x + 150$. $5x = 50 \implies x = 10$. Wahi result aaya, bas thoda zyada likhna pada. questions_hin.q_hi: In an examination, (A + 6)% of the students failed in Mathematics and (A - 8)% failed in Science. 28% of the students failed in both the subjects. If the percentage of students who passed in both the subjects was 50%, then what is the value of A?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, total bachhe humesha $100\%$ hote hain. Jo dono subjects me pass hue wo $50\%$ de rakhe hain, toh iska matlab jo kisi na kisi ek me (ya dono me) fail hue wo total $100 - 50 = 50\%$ honge. Seedha set theory yaad kar.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Universal set wala formula laga aur equation turant solve kar de!

Mathematically :-
$$n(M \cup S) = n(M) + n(S) - n(M \cap S)$$
$$50 = (A + 6) + (A - 8) - 28$$
$$50 = 2A - 30 \implies 2A = 80 \implies A = 40$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Venn diagram ke logic se only math aur only science ke fail nikal ke total bana le.

Mathematically :-
$$\text{Only Math} = (A + 6) - 28 = A - 22$$
$$\text{Only Sci} = (A - 8) - 28 = A - 36$$
$$\text{Total Fail} = (A - 22) + (A - 36) + 28 = 2A - 30$$
$$2A - 30 = 50 \implies A = 40$$

Exam Takeaway: Har baar Venn diagram draw karne me time barbaad mat kiya kar, seedha union wala set formula dimag me rakha kar!

questions_hin.q_hi: In an examination every question correctly answered fetches two marks and for every question wrongly answered one mark is deducted. Anusha and Preet took the examination. Anusha attempted a certain number of question and 20\% of them went wrong. Preet attempted a certain number of questions and 10\% of the questions attempted by him went wrong. Anusha got 33 marks more than the pass mark and Preet got 48 marks more than the pass mark. Anusha and Preet together attempted 100 questions. What is the pass mark of the examination?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: Expected Value & Divisibility.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, jab bhi correct aur incorrect ka percentage given ho, toh fraction se ek "Base Score Unit" nikal le. Uss unit se seedha divisibility check kar ke options eliminate karna sabse BEST approach hai. Warna original mock solution wale expected value (net marks) se linear equation banegi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Option Picking with Divisibility. Anusha ka 20\% (1/5) wrong hai, yani har 5 attempt ki packet me 4 right aur 1 wrong. Uska 1 packet ka marks = $4 \times (+2) + 1 \times (-1) = 7$ marks. Preet ka 10\% (1/10) wrong hai, yani har 10 attempt me 9 right aur 1 wrong. Uska 1 packet ka marks = $9 \times (+2) + 1 \times (-1) = 17$ marks. Total scores definitely 7 aur 17 ke multiples honge. Option se pass marks 37 uthao.

Mathematically :-
$$A_{score} = 37 + 33 = 70 \ (10 \times 7 \text{ units} \rightarrow 50 \text{ Qs}) \\ P_{score} = 37 + 48 = 85 \ (5 \times 17 \text{ units} \rightarrow 50 \text{ Qs}) \\ Total = 50 + 50 = 100 \text{ (Verified)}$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Original Mock Solution. Har attempt ka ek average expected mark nikal le decimals me.

Mathematically :-
$$A_{net} = 0.8(2) - 0.2(1) = 1.4 \\ P_{net} = 0.9(2) - 0.1(1) = 1.7 \\ P_{score} - A_{score} = 48 - 33 = 15 \\ 1.7(100 - A) - 1.4A = 15 \\ 170 - 3.1A = 15 \rightarrow 3.1A = 155 \rightarrow A = 50 \\ Pass = 50 \times 1.4 - 33 = 37$$

Exam Takeaway: Hamesha percentage ko packet ratio me tod kar unit score nikal le. Phir sidha options me margin add karke divisibility test kar. Ye DIRECT approach time 10x bacha legi bina kisi variable assume kiye!

questions_hin.q_hi: Every day, a wholesale fruit vendor sells $60 \%$ of his total stock. From the remaining stock, he donates $25 \%$ to a local orphanage, and then $20 \%$ of the rest gets spoiled overnight. If exactly 3720 fruits were spoiled over the first two nights combined, how many fruits did he start with on the first day?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, yahan lagatar 3 reductions ho rahe hain har roz. Pehle $60 \%$ bika, fir bache hue ka $25 \%$ daan kiya, fir jo bacha uska $20 \%$ kharab hua. Fractions ka series lamba hai, isliye $100$ ke bajaye $10000$ base maan le taaki calculations decimals me na phase.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Total stock ko ek aisi unit maan lo jo har fraction se easily divide ho jaye. Phir step-by-step successive decrease laga do.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Let Initial Stock} = 10000 \text{ units} \\ \text{Day 1: Sells } 60 \% \implies \text{Remaining} = 4000 \\ \text{Donates } 25 \% \text{ of } 4000 = 1000 \implies \text{Rest} = 3000 \\ \text{Night 1 Spoils} = 20 \% \text{ of } 3000 = 600 \\ \text{Day 2 Starts with} = 3000 - 600 = 2400 \text{ units} \\ \text{Day 2: Sells } 60 \% \text{ of } 2400 = 1440 \implies \text{Remaining} = 960 \\ \text{Donates } 25 \% \text{ of } 960 = 240 \implies \text{Rest} = 720 \\ \text{Night 2 Spoils} = 20 \% \text{ of } 720 = 144 \\ \text{Total Spoiled} = 600 + 144 = 744 \text{ units} \\ 744 \text{ units} = 3720 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = 5 \\ \text{Total initial fruits} = 10000 \times 5 = 50000 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Multipliers ko club karke single remaining fraction nikal lo jisse daily calculation aadhi ho jaye.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Let Initial Stock} = X \\ \text{Daily Rest Fraction (before spoiling)} = (1 - 0.60) \times (1 - 0.25) \\ = 0.40 \times 0.75 = 0.30 \\ \text{Night 1 Spoiled} = 20 \% \text{ of } 0.30X = 0.06X \\ \text{Remaining for Day 2} = 0.30X - 0.06X = 0.24X \\ \text{Night 2 Spoiled} = 20 \% \text{ of } (0.30 \times 0.24X) = 0.0144X \\ \text{Total Spoiled} = 0.06X + 0.0144X = 0.0744X \\ 0.0744X = 3720 \implies X = \frac{3720}{0.0744} = 50000 $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab din me multi-step reductions hon, toh un sabko club karke ek single remaining multiplier ($0.4 \times 0.75 = 0.3$) bana lena chahiye. Isse next day ki chain equation bohot choti aur fast ho jati hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique - Actual Base calculation):
Deepak spends 75%, so saves 25% (\\frac{1}{4}). Base Income = $7500 \\times 4 = 30000$.
Karan spends 80%, so saves 20% (\\frac{1}{5}). Base Income = $7500 \\times 5 = 37500$.
Sum of Incomes = $30000 + 37500 = 67500$.
Sanjay's Income = $\\frac{67500}{3} = 22500$.
Sanjay spends $\\frac{7}{9}$, so saves $\\frac{2}{9}$.
Savings = $\\frac{2}{9} \\times 22500 = 5000$.

Method 2 (Teri 'Zeher' Ratio Approach):
Savings barabar hain, seedha ratios equate kar!
$D \\times 25\\% = K \\times 20\\% \\Rightarrow \\frac{D}{K} = \\frac{4}{5}$. Total = 9 units.
Sanjay's savings in units = $9 \\times \\frac{1}{3} \\times \\frac{2}{9} = \\frac{2}{3}$ units.
Ab real value se link kar: Deepak's saving = $4 \\times \\frac{1}{4} = 1$ unit.
Question ke hisaab se, $1 \\text{ unit} = 7500$.
Sanjay's saving = $7500 \\times \\frac{2}{3} = 5000$. Dono hi method 15 second wale hain, zero algebraic variables ka masterstroke!

questions_hin.q_hi: A student appeared in 6 papers. The maximum marks are the same for each paper. His marks in these papers are in the proportion 5 : 6 : 7 : 8 : 9 : 10. Overall he scored 60%. In how many papers he received less than 60% marks?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling / Deviation

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Data proportion me diya hai aur final relative constraint (60%) par focus hai. Total marks obtained ratio ke terms me jodo, waha se maximum marks ki imaginary value nikal lo.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Sum of scores = $5+6+7+8+9+10 = 45x$. Ye 45x overall max marks ka 60% hai. Yaani $60\% = 45x \implies 100\% (Total Max) = \frac{45x}{60} \times 100 = 75x$. 6 papers ka Total Max 75x hai, aur sab equal hain. Toh 1 paper ka Max = $\frac{75x}{6} = 12.5x$. Kisi subject me 60% se kam aane ka constraint check karna hai. 12.5x ka 60% hota hai 7.5x. Toh kin subjects me 7.5x se kam hai? Pehle teen (5, 6, 7). Answer 3.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Algebraically assume Total Max = 600. Then 60% = 360. $45x = 360 \implies x=8$. Marks are 40, 48, 56, 64, 72, 80. Each paper max = 100. 60% of 100 = 60. Marks < 60 are 40, 48, 56 (3 papers). Same logic!

Best Exam Approach: Method 1 me ek ratio base calculation hai jo dimag me jaldi process hota hai.

Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change (The Chain Reaction) - TRICK IDENTIFICATION

Aankhein khuli rakh paper me! Mathematically :- $$ \text{Increase per day} = \frac{\text{Weekly Increase}}{7} \\ \text{Increase} = \frac{25200}{7} = 3600 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Agar tum concept pe gaye toh net effect nikaloge, fir equation solve karoge. Itna bada trap bicha rakha hai wahan mat fans jana. Mathematically :- $$ \text{Net } \% = -15 + 35 - \frac{15 \times 35}{100} = +14.75\% \\ 14.75\% \text{ of Total} = 25200 \text{ (Useless calc)} \\ \text{Per day} = \frac{25200}{7} = 3600 $$

questions_hin.q_hi: A fraction $\frac{3}{5}$ is decreased by $\frac{2}{5}$. The resulting fraction is then increased by 20%.\n\nWhat is the percentage decrease/increase in the value of the original fraction?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, base me 5 hai dono jagah. $ rac{3}{5}$ me se $ rac{2}{5}$ gaya toh bacha $ rac{1}{5}$. Ab $ rac{1}{5}$ ko 20% (yani khud ka $ rac{1}{5}$th) badhana hai. Seedha seedha base ko 25 dimaag me soch aur numerators ko 15 aur 6 padh. 15 se 6 hua, matlab 9 ka loss 15 par. $ rac{9}{15}$ seedha 60% hota hai! Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Base same kar lo taaki fractions integers jaise behave karein. Mathematically :-
$ ext{Original} = rac{3}{5} = rac{15}{25}$
$ ext{New} = ( rac{3}{5} - rac{2}{5}) imes 1.2 = rac{1}{5} imes rac{6}{5} = rac{6}{25}$
$\% ext{ Decrease} = rac{15 - 6}{15} imes 100 = 60\%$ Method 2 (Concept Builder): Basic se chalte hain. Pehle original fraction me se fraction minus karo, fir jo aaye usko 20% increase karo (multiply by $ rac{6}{5}$). Mathematically :-
$ ext{Original} = rac{3}{5}$
$ ext{After subtraction} = rac{3}{5} - rac{2}{5} = rac{1}{5}$
$ ext{After 20\% increase} = rac{1}{5} imes (1 + rac{20}{100}) = rac{1}{5} imes rac{6}{5} = rac{6}{25}$
$ ext{Absolute Change} = rac{3}{5} - rac{6}{25} = rac{15}{25} - rac{6}{25} = rac{9}{25}$
$ ext{Percentage Change} = rac{ rac{9}{25}}{ rac{15}{25}} imes 100 = rac{9}{15} imes 100 = 60\%$ Exam Takeaway: Is type ke questions me "decreased by a fraction" aur "decreased by a percentage" ka phrasing hi trap hota hai. Hamesha final aur initial fraction ka base same kar lo (jaise yahan humne dono ko 25 bana liya), toh calculation seconds me muh-zabani ho jayegi.

Base EqualizationWhenever comparing fractions to find percentage change, equalize their denominators.
Fractional MultiplierFor a 20% increase, directly multiply by $ rac{6}{5}$ instead of calculating 20% and adding it back.

questions_hin.q_hi: In company A, the number of male employees is $71.42\%$ of the total employees. The total number of employees in company B is $14.28\%$ less than that in company A. If the difference between male and female employees in company A is $(x+12)$ and the total employees in company B is 84, find the value of x.
questions_hin.s_hi:
The "Pen-Free" Observation First:

Dekh bhai, fractions strong hone chahiye. $14.28\% = \frac{1}{7}$ and $71.42\% = \frac{5}{7}$. Bas en fraction scale par relation bitha aur ek line me solve kar!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):

Mathematically :-

$$ 14.28\% = \frac{1}{7}, \quad 71.42\% = \frac{5}{7} \\ B = \left(1 - \frac{1}{7}\right)A = \frac{6}{7}A \\ 84 = \frac{6}{7}A \implies A = 98 \\ \text{Males (A)} = \frac{5}{7} \times 98 = 70 \\ \text{Females (A)} = 98 - 70 = 28 \\ \text{Diff} = 70 - 28 = 42 \\ (x + 12) = 42 \implies x = 30 $$

Exam Takeaway: Standard percentages ko directly fraction me todna TCS exams me life-saver hai.

questions_hin.q_hi: The number of peacocks in a bird sanctuary was P in the year 2000. The number decreased by $10\%$ in the next decade and increased by $50\%$ in the decade after that. If the difference between the number of peacocks in the years 2020 and 2000 is 5250, and it increased by $36\%$ in the next half decade, then what is the number of peacocks in the year 2025?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, pehle gira fir utha. Net successive change nikal, P ki value aayegi. Uske baad 2025 ki value aayegi jo 1.36 se multiply karke banegi, jiska DS 9 HOGA COZ +18/50 SO opt C&D elmnt and unit digit pakad lena hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Net effect = 0.9 x 1.5 = 1.35. Yani 35% bada. $35\% = 5250$ toh $100\% (P) = 15000$. 2020 me = $15000 \times 1.35 = 20250$. Naya 36% bada, $20250 \times 1.36$. Last digit zero ke baad 4 aayega, option B me 40 hai, seedha tick maar!

Mathematically :-
$\text{Net}_1 = 0.9 \times 1.5 = 1.35$
$\text{Diff} = 35\% = 5250 \implies 100\% = 15000$
$P_{2020} = 15000 \times 1.35 = 20250$
$P_{2025} = 20250 \times 1.36 = 27540$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): $P - P(0.9)(1.5)$ likh ke formula banayega, subtract karega toh bhi end me calculation unit digit se hi fast hogi.

Mathematically :-
$P(1.5)(0.9) - P = 5250$
$0.35P = 5250 \implies P = 15000$
$P_{2025} = 15000(1.35)(1.36) = 27540$

Exam Takeaway: Pure multiplication mat kar, Unit digit aur Digital Sum hamesha bachate hain successive problems me.

questions_hin.q_hi: Raman saves $x\%$ of her income. If her income increases by $16\%$ and expenditure increases by $10\%$ then her savings increased by $50\%$. What is the value of x?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: 3. JSM / Deviation (Cross-Product Alligation)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, Income me bas $16\%$ ka hike hai, aur Saving achanak $50\%$ ud gayi, jabki Expenditure me halka sa $10\%$ change hai. Iska seedha matlab hai initially saving ka share total income me bahut kam tha.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Seedha Alligation laga! Exp ($10\%$) aur Sav ($50\%$) mix hokar total Income ($16\%$) ka change banate hain. Secondon ka game hai!

Mathematically :-
$$ E = 10\\% , \\ S = 50\\% , \\ I = 16\\% \\\\ Ratio (E:S) = (50-16) : (16-10) \\\\ = 34 : 6 = 17 : 3 \\\\ Total \\ I = 17 + 3 = 20 \\\\ S\\% = \\frac{3}{20} \\times 100 = 15\\% $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Maan le Total Income $= 100$, Sav $= x$, Exp $= 100-x$. Equation set kar: Naya Exp $+$ Nayi Sav $=$ Nayi Income. Par ye gadha majdoori hai.

Mathematically :-
$$ I = 100, \\ S = x, \\ E = 100-x \\\\ E_{new} + S_{new} = I_{new} \\\\ 1.1(100-x) + 1.5x = 116 \\\\ 110 - 1.1x + 1.5x = 116 \\\\ 0.4x = 6 \\\\ x = 15\\% $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab bhi $3$ components (A, B, aur unka combined total) ka percentage increase/decrease diya ho, Alligation se fast kuch nahi hota!

questions_hin.q_hi: Everyday a vegetable vendor sells $1/2$ of his total stock. $10 \%$ of the remaining stock overnight gets spoiled. If 1983 vegetables spoiled over 3 nights in total, then how many vegetables did he start with on the first day?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change

Pen-Free Observation: Har roz half sell hota hai aur fir bache hue half ka $10 \%$ (yani remaining part) spoil hota hai. Fraction chain lagatar change ho rahi hai toh calculation thodi lengthy lag sakti hai, best hai koi constant value assume karna.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Denominators dekhte hue initial value ko 8000 ka koi multiple maan lo ($2 \times 10 \times 2 \times 10$ series ke hisab se) taaki points me calculations na jaye.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Let Initial Stock} = 8000 \text{ units} \\ \text{Day 1:} \text{ sells } 4000, \text{ Rem } 4000. \text{ Night 1 spoils } 10 \% = 400 \\ \text{Day 2:} \text{ Starts with } 3600. \text{ Sells } 1800, \text{ Rem } 1800. \text{ Night 2 spoils } 10 \% = 180 \\ \text{Day 3:} \text{ Starts with } 1620. \text{ Sells } 810, \text{ Rem } 810. \text{ Night 3 spoils } 10 \% = 81 \\ \text{Total Spoiled} = 400 + 180 + 81 = 661 \text{ units} \\ 661 \text{ units} = 1983 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = 3 \\ \text{Total initial fruits} = 8000 \times 3 = 24000 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Pure fraction method laga kar $X$ le kar solve karna.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Let Initial} = X \\ \text{Night 1 Spoiled} = 10 \% \text{ of } \frac{X}{2} = \frac{400}{8000}X \\ \text{Remaining Day 2 Start} = \frac{X}{2} - \frac{X}{20} = \frac{9}{20}X \\ \text{Night 2 Spoiled} = 10 \% \text{ of } (\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{9}{20}X) = \frac{180}{8000}X \\ \text{Remaining Day 3 Start} = \frac{9}{40}X - \frac{9}{400}X = \frac{81}{400}X \\ \text{Night 3 Spoiled} = 10 \% \text{ of } (\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{81}{400}X) = \frac{81}{8000}X \\ \text{Total Spoiled} = (\frac{400 + 180 + 81}{8000})X = \frac{661}{8000}X \\ \frac{661}{8000}X = 1983 \implies X = 24000 $$

Exam Takeaway: Fraction wale successive sawalo me LCM based assumption sabse best hack hota hai. 8000 man-ne se saara problem purely integers me handle ho gaya.

questions_hin.q_hi: Suhani pays tax at the rate of $30\%$ on her entire income of 90,000 and Ritika pays tax at the rate of $40\%$ on her entire income of y. If the total rate of tax on their combined income becomes $37\%$, then what is the value of y?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: 4. Cross-Product Method (Alligation)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, jab do alag alag percentages combine hoke ek overall percentage de rahe ho, tab bina soche Alligation thok dena chahiye Use JSM jab BASE RATIO given ho.Jab question mein tujhe ratio of quantity (jaise Male:Female ratio, ya Income:Saving ratio) already diya ho, aur tujhe Overall Average nikaalna ho, ya koi ek missing individual value nikaalni ho. JSM is all about shifting extra deviation across a known base ratio..

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Suhani 30, Ritika 40. Mix bana 37. Cross me difference le. $40-37 = 3$, aur $37-30 = 7$. Ratio income ka 3:7 aaya. Suhani (3 unit) = 90,000 toh Ritika (7 unit) = 2,10,000. Sidha oraly solve!

Mathematically :-
$\text{Ratio} = (40-37) : (37-30) = 3:7$
$3 \text{ unit} = 90000$
$7 \text{ unit} = 210000$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Weighted average $30(90k) + 40(y) = 37(90k + y)$ banake equation ko balance kar. Wahi answer aayega par time khayega.

Mathematically :-
$30\%(90000) + 40\%(y) = 37\%(90000 + y)$
$27000 + 0.4y = 33300 + 0.37y$
$0.03y = 6300 \implies y = 210000$

Exam Takeaway: Combined averages ke har sawal ka baap Alligation hai, usko base par use karna seekh.

questions_hin.q_hi: In a cricket series, Team A had a winning rate of $70\%$ after playing x matches. Then they lost 20 matches consecutively, and their winning rate fell to $50\%$. Find the total matches played by Team A before the losing streak?

questions_hin.q_hi: The water volume in a reservoir increases by $16 \frac{2}{3}\%$ in January, decreases by 20,000 liters in February, and increases by $25\%$ in March. If the final volume is exactly $25\%$ more than the initial volume, find the total increment in the volume during January.
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, final $25\%$ zyada hai aur last step (March) bhi $25\%$ increase hai. Iska matlab March start hone se pehle volume wapas Initial ke barabar thi. Seedha mind me strike karna chahiye ki February end me volume P thi . Ye Result hai Direct yaad karlo log isko short tirick bolenge baad me 🫠.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Reverse Gear.

Mathematically :-

$$ Final = 1.25P \\ Before\_Mar = \frac{1.25P}{1.25} = P \\ Before\_Feb = P + 20000 \\ Jan\_Inc = 16 \frac{2}{3}\% = \frac{1}{6} \\ \frac{7P}{6} = P + 20000 \\ \frac{P}{6} = 20000 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Forward Equation.

Mathematically :-

$$ \left(\frac{7P}{6} - 20000\right) \times \frac{5}{4} = \frac{5P}{4} \\ \frac{7P}{6} - 20000 = P \\ \frac{P}{6} = 20000 $$

Exam Takeaway: Language ghumane ke liye exam me volume ya fuel de dega, par percentages ko aas paas ki absolute value se link karna same rahega.

questions_hin.q_hi: In an examination, there were two papers, X and Y, and the maximum mark in each of the two papers was 20. However, the weights assigned to papers X and Y were in the ratio 3: 2, respectively. Rohan scored 18 out of 20 in Paper X and an overall $70\%$ in the examination. How much did he score in Paper Y out of 20?

Core Conceptual Tool: 3. JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method) / Deviation

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, X me $90\%$ laaya hai ($18/20$), aur overall sirf $70\%$ chahiye. Matlab Y me definitely $70\%$ se kafi kam score aayega!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): JSM ka tagda use karenge yahan. X ka score hai $90\%$, aur target hai $70\%$. X kitna extra laya? $+20\%$. X ka weight $3$ hai, toh total extra hua $3 \times 20 = +60$. Ye $+60$ compensate karna padega Y ko jiska weight $2$ hai. Toh Y ka deviation aayega $-\frac{60}{2} = -30\%$. Y ko base $70\%$ se $30\%$ kam lana padega, yani $40\%$. Ab $20$ marks ka $40\%$ kitna hota hai? Seedha $8$!

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Weighted average ka desi formula laga le. $\frac{W_1 \times S_1 + W_2 \times S_2}{W_1 + W_2} = \text{Overall}$. Yani $\frac{3 \times 90 + 2 \times Y}{5} = 70$. Equation solve karega toh $270 + 2Y = 350 \implies Y = 40\%$. Phir $20$ ka $40\%$ nikal.

Exam Takeaway: Average aur mixture ke questions me formula lagane se acha JSM (Deviation) lagao, calculations aadhi ho jayengi.

questions_hin.q_hi: $25\%$ of half of x is equal to $2.5$ times of ($30\%$ of one-fourth of y). Then x is what percent more or less than y?
questions_hin.s_hi:
The "Pen-Free" Observation First:

Dekh bhai, percentages ko seedha fraction me likh. Equation ko ek line me scale kar aur cut-pit shuru kar de.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):

Mathematically :-

$$ \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{2} \times x = 2.5 \times \left( \frac{3}{10} \times \frac{1}{4} \times y \right) \\ \frac{x}{8} = \frac{25}{10} \times \frac{3}{40} \times y \\ \frac{x}{8} = \frac{3}{16} y \\ \frac{x}{y} = \frac{3}{16} \times 8 = \frac{3}{2} = 1.5 \\ x = 1.5y \implies x \text{ is } 50\% \text{ more than } y $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab numbers fractional ya percentage form me ho, equality set karke sidha ratio nikalna fastest hack hai.

questions_hin.q_hi: In Veeru Bhai Pvt. limited company 60% of the employees are men and 48% of the employees are engineers and 66.66% of these are men. The percentage of women who are <u>not</u> engineers:
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, jab aise percentages of percentages me exam setter khel raha ho, toh total employees ko aankh band karke $100$ maan le. Language ki trap ye hai ki base kiske reference me pucha gaya hai, wo dekhna bahut zaroori hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Total $100$ leke branches bana aur jo manga hai wo seedha nikal!

Mathematically :-
$$\text{Total} = 100 \implies \text{Men} = 60, \text{Women} = 40$$
$$\text{Total Engg} = 48$$
$$\text{Men Engg} = \frac{2}{3} \times 48 = 32$$
$$\text{Women Engg} = 48 - 32 = 16$$
$$\text{Non-Engg Women} = 40 - 16 = 24$$
$$\text{Req } \% = \frac{24}{40} \times 100 = 60\%$$
